concerns: Run 4 (LightGBM, all+agent) has the best PR-AUC at 0.7381, but its lead over run 2 (random forest, 0.704) is 0.034, below one fold SD (about 0.061-0.066). The gain is not distinguishable from noise.

Run 1 (logistic, no_size) at 0.6809 is within one SD of every other run, so the simplest model is competitive. Run 2 is only 0.023 better, which is also under one SD. By the simplicity rule logistic would be the choice, but run 2 is a modest, defensible step up. Neither is clearly separated from the other.
Fold SDs of 0.06-0.076 on 5,410 providers with about 506 positives mean the differences between runs are small compared with the noise. Further tuning is unlikely to give a reliable gain.

The ROC-AUC of about 0.94 is high and almost identical across all models. PR-AUC of 0.68-0.74 and precision@50 of 0.74-0.80 are strong for provider-level data. This may mean the label reflects a simple rule or an artefact of claim volume or size features rather than confirmed fraud. The origin of the label is undocumented, so the model may be reproducing the labelling process instead of detecting fraud.
The size features add little: run 1 without them is close to run 2 with them. That is reassuring about volume leakage, but it was not tested in a controlled comparison.
The 19 agent features are aggregates built from claim-level data and may encode label-related structure. The evidence that they help is weak, and the best run (4) uses them.
Folds should be grouped so that no provider or related entity appears in both train and test. Claims span 2008-2009 and no temporal validation was done, so performance on future data is unknown.
The audit queue holds about 100 providers, but only precision@50 is reported. Precision at about 100 is not shown.

review.split_comment: A stratified provider-level 5-fold CV keeps each provider in one fold, which is appropriate since the features are per-provider aggregates. The label is undocumented and may reflect prior audit outcomes, so scores should be read as suspicion ranking. Report PR-AUC along with precision at about 100 providers. The cross-provider duplicate feature should be checked for computation across folds.

1.rationale: Regularized linear baseline without size features, so the ranking is not just provider volume. Class weighting handles the 9% positive rate. Gives a stable reference point.

2.rationale: Bagged trees with moderate leaf size are robust on noisy, undocumented labels. All 63 features show the ceiling from including size.

3.rationale: Low-capacity boosting with strong regularization on size-neutral features plus agent features. No reweighting keeps probabilities well calibrated for top-100 precision.

4.rationale: Higher-capacity boosting on the full feature set with class weights, testing whether extra capacity and agent features improve PR-AUC beyond the regularized variants.
